question: What three types of signs are required at an interchange exit-ramp terminal where wrong-way entry could inadvertently occur?
model_answer: Direct Answer: Based on the available evidence, the three types of regulatory signs shown at an exit-ramp termination to deter wrong-way entry are DO NOT ENTER (R5-1), WRONG WAY (R5-1a), and ONE WAY (R6-1/R6-2) signs, as illustrated in Figure 2B-15. However, the text evidence supplied does not include the actual Standard provision (from Section 2B.48) that mandates these signs, so I cannot quote the mandatory "shall" language verbatim; the requirement can only be confirmed here through the illustrative figure and related supporting pages. Standards (mandatory): - No Standard provision stating the three required sign types at exit-ramp terminals is included in the supplied text evidence. (The provided Standards — Section 2J.07 §2 on Specific Service ramp signs and Section 2E.21 §2 on interchange guide signs — address different topics and do not establish the wrong-way-deterrence sign requirement.) Guidance (recommended): - "To minimize wrong-way movements onto freeway or expressway exit ramps, Street Name signs should not be used at the intersection of a freeway or expressway exit ramp with the crossroad to display the name of the freeway or expressway to traffic on the crossroad." This is a related, but distinct, wrong-way countermeasure. Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Figure 2B-15 depicts DO NOT ENTER, WRONG WAY, and ONE WAY signs (along with STOP or YIELD signs and pavement markings) positioned at an exit-ramp termination facing potential wrong-way traffic. - [Image 2] Shows Figure 2B-15 in its full-page context (Section 2B.48), again illustrating DO NOT ENTER, WRONG WAY, and ONE WAY signs at the exit-ramp terminal. - [Image 3] Page 150 (Section 2B.46) lists the DO NOT ENTER, WRONG WAY, ONE WAY, and related signs (R5-1, R5-1a, R6-1, R6-2) in Figure 2B-13 and requires the DO NOT ENTER sign at "the intersection of an interchange exit ramp with a crossroad as specified in Section 2B.48." - [Image 4] Page 29 (table of contents) lists Figure 2B-15, "Example of Application of Regulatory Signing and Pavement Markings at an Exit Ramp Termination to Deter Wrong-Way Entry." - [Image 5] Page 297 (Figure 2D-18) includes a note directing readers to "Section 2B.48 and Figure 2B-15 for an example of regulatory signing and pavement markings at an exit ramp termination to deter wrong-way entry." Citations: - Section 2D.45 Guidance §3 (p.247) - Figure 2B-15 (p.112) - Page 153 - Page 150 - Page 29 - Page 297
gold_answer: At least one ONE WAY sign for each crossroad travel direction, at least one DO NOT ENTER sign near the downstream end of the exit ramp, and at least one WRONG WAY sign on the exit ramp facing wrong-way road users are required.
